notes: Full test (pods/ROUTINE.md §5.4) : accroche neuve de la famille « Paintings That… » de @mariadianatudor (« Paintings That Devour My Soul », 36,9 k vues, 29/10), même gabarit, même musique. Œuvres du domaine public au Met (Open Access, CC0), aucune déjà postée ce mois-ci. Faits vérifiés : Van Gogh, Roses (1890) : peint à Saint-Rémy en mai 1890 avant le départ pour Auvers (16 mai) ; mort le 29 juillet 1890 ; roses à l'origine roses, le pigment rouge (laque) a pâli (notice du Met). Manet, La Famille Monet dans son jardin à Argenteuil (1874) : Camille et Jean Monet, Monet au jardin ; Renoir peint la même scène à côté (National Gallery of Art, Washington) ; Camille morte en septembre 1879 à 32 ans. Chardin, Les Bulles de savon (vers 1733-34) : au moins trois versions (Met, LACMA, NGA) ; thème de la vanité. Rembrandt, Autoportrait (1660) : 54 ans ; faillite en 1656, maison et collection vendues (1657-58). Slide Artura : version `cta C`, son logo sous le paragraphe, jamais une capture. Couverture : Seedream (visiteurs de dos, le tableau flou).

en.titre: Paintings That Feel Like A Goodbye

en.texte: was painted in May 1890, in Van Gogh's last days at the asylum in Saint-Rémy, just before he left for Auvers. He died two months later. The roses were pink; the red pigment has faded, and today they look almost white.

en.titre: The Monet Family in Their Garden
en.texte: shows Camille Monet and her son resting on the grass in Argenteuil in the summer of 1874, while Monet tends the garden. Manet painted it in an afternoon, and Renoir arrived and painted the same scene beside him. Camille died five years later, at 32.
is a young man blowing a bubble that is about to burst. For Chardin's time, a soap bubble meant one thing: how short life is. He painted the scene at least three times around 1733.

was painted in 1660, when Rembrandt was 54 and had lost almost everything: his house and his collection had been sold after his bankruptcy. He looks at us without hiding anything. Artura gives me one painting a day and the story behind it; this one stayed with me.
